questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: The most important aspects for me, to why I choose the destination Narva, was to get better at Russian and that the teaching on my exchange took place in Russian.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: It required quite a bit of time to find all the information I needed.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: I didn't get that much assistance, but I figured it out myself.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: There was only one room available at the dormitory, which I did not get. I applied one month before I had to go on exchange and got a reply 1,5 weeks before I had to go. This was very stressful, but I managed to find an apartment a few days before my departure, which I was incredibly happy about!

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: I would recommend to everyone to find an apartment, because of they few rooms available in the dormitory.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: I had to figure out how to register myself, there wasn't much help to be had.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: Not that much.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I got all the classes that I wanted, so I was happy about that.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: It is possible to figure it out on your own!

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: Some courses were more difficult than others but overall I think the level of the courses was high, but this contributed to making the teaching more exciting.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: The teaching differed in that there was far less reading as homework, but way more tests.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer: History and Culture of Russia, Russian Culture in a Context of the Intercultural Communication, Linguistic Text Analysis, Russian Language Functional Stylistics, Russian Grammar II Level B2, Russian Lexicology, Phraseology and Lexicography, Contemporary Russian Literature and Cinematography in the Studies of Russian as a Foreign Language, Practical Russian, Accuracy of Russian Language Speech I.

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I would recommend the course "Practical Russian" in that the course was at a lower language level than the other courses, which makes it easier to follow the lessons.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: None.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Grocery shopping was more expensive than I expected, but still much cheaper than Danish prices. Bolt (taxi) was very cheap as well as Bolt scooters.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: There weren't really any social or athletic activities at university. In general Narva is a very small and quiet town and not much happens there.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I joined the local gym and went there a lot with a friend. It was really good! the subscription was not expensive and it was a good fintess center.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: I visited stockholm for a weekend as it is close to Estonia and the plane tickets were always cheap. Otherwise, you can go to Tallinn and Tartu at the weekends, these cities are bigger and you can do more things there than in Narva.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: For me personally it was easy, because of my Russian background and knowledge of the Russian language.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: At first people can seem quite "closed off" but as soon as you get to know them, they are really nice!

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: None.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The language.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: Find a place to stay in good time. even if they don't seem very social at first, don't give up. be prepared to find things to do yourself, as there are not very many things you can do in the city, such as clubs, bars, cafes/restaurants, shopping, attractions.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: No.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: To experience and live in a foreign culture. For my part, my Russian has improved even more after spending a semester in a Russian-speaking city.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Being away from home for 4,5 months.

questions.question: Any other comments?
questions.answer: No

questions.question: Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
